**My pick for RV boondocking under $1,000 is the <Entity category="product" value="BLUETTI AC200L" disambig="2048Wh LiFePO4 portable power station"/>**, particularly if you want to power your RV through its shore-power connection.

<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station product photo" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="148px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    <text weight="medium">BLUETTI AC200L — Best for RV integration</text>
    <title size="xl">$854.05</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Reported discounted price; regular $899 with code AFF5OFF</text>
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">2,048Wh LiFePO4 · 2,400W AC output · 1,200W solar input · Built-in TT-30 RV outlet</text>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Seller: BLUETTI Official US Store · Listed in stock when checked by source</text>
    <text size="sm"><Link url="https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l" title="View offer"/></text>
  </box>
</row>

The biggest advantage is its **built-in 30-amp-style RV outlet**. You can connect compatible RV shore-power equipment without relying solely on household AC sockets. However, its 2,400W inverter provides approximately 20A at 120V, not a full 30A service. <Cite ref="turn607949view0"/>

## How it compares

| Power station | Capacity | Output | Listed price |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | $854* |
| <Entity category="product" value="Jackery Explorer 2000 v2"/> | 2,042Wh | 2,200W | $999 |
| <Entity category="product" value="EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max"/> | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | $999 |
| <Entity category="product" value="Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2"/> | 1,024Wh | 2,000W | $699 |

<caption>*Prices are reported by the supplied 2026 search results, not independently verified live offers. The BLUETTI price includes a reported affiliate discount.</caption>

## What it can realistically power

- **Good for:** RV lighting, water pumps, electronics, a compressor fridge, and occasional coffee-maker use.
- **With solar:** Its 1,200W maximum solar input offers substantial recharging potential, depending on panels and sunlight.
- **Not ideal for:** Running rooftop air conditioning overnight or supplying a full 30A RV electrical load.

For a weekend trailer, the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 is a lighter, less expensive alternative. For extended boondocking, I would favor the roughly 2kWh BLUETTI or Jackery instead. <Cite ref="turn607949view0"/>

**Bottom line:** Choose the BLUETTI AC200L if RV hookup convenience matters most. Choose the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 if portability matters more; the search results list it at 43.5 lb.

One question would help narrow this further: **Are you trying to power your RV's existing 30A hookup, or just individual appliances like a fridge, Starlink, and coffee maker?**
